result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers handle radius well: zero by default, plus one named exception for true circles. A is more ready to use: it gives a paste-ready CSS block with real values and clearly separates raised elements (4px offset) from overlays (8px offset). B fits the 'basically no animation' brand better, with 0ms as the default and a single 100ms linear duration, and it says plainly what it leaves out (entrance, scroll-linked and looping motion, gradients, sm/md/lg). B also flags a contrast risk with the tomato-red focus ring, but it doesn't spell out how an overlay should look. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers keep radius at zero with a deliberate round exception, and both build depth from hard offsets instead of blur. A matches the brand's 'basically no animation' better: it uses one 100ms linear duration, defaults to 0ms and explicitly leaves out entrance and looping motion. B adds a second duration and a cubic-bezier easing. B is more concrete and ready to paste, and it separates raised, overlay and pressed elevation more clearly, so the strengths balance out.
